analysis.title: US Market Intelligence Morning Briefing, October 27, 2026
key_insights: JPM US Market Intel stays tactically bullish. SPX lost 2.4% over the last 2 weeks and is -36bp month to date, with 8 of 11 sectors positive. Basis for the view: flash PMIs point to ~5% annualized real growth for a second month, and about a quarter of the SPX has reported with no dips to pre-season forecasts (~13% revenue growth, ~30% EPS growth, ~15% margins).

Yesterday re-established the AI theme. Next catalysts are the ORCL investor day and MegaCap Tech earnings (AMZN, GOOG, INTC, MSFT) this week. If these are read as bullish, momentum could build into the post-midterm positive seasonal period and a year-end rally.

Client conversations list what had to happen for investors to re-engage with AI: hyperscaler capex confirmation, positioning wash out, capital markets filings, a retail or buyback bid, and the passage of time toward positive seasonality. Parts have occurred and Memory/Semis responded positively to yesterday's filings.
The positioning signal is less clear because there has not been a complete positioning washout, even though sentiment is firmly in the Fear region.

Feroli expects the Fed to hold this week with two hawkish dissents from Hammack and Logan, and sees a risk that Kashkari also dissents. He expects the statement to say that policy will deliver a timely return to price stability.

On the press conference, Feroli says Chair Warsh must explain why the committee hiked after a two-tenths core PCE print in September but is now holding after an expected three-tenths print. The likely message is that the Committee is biased to hike but wants more time to see the effect of last month's hike.

US Market Intel expects Fed-driven volatility could extend into the following week as other Fed speakers are more forthcoming. Focus is on how policymakers reassess the December meeting and the 2027 path after the hawkish September inflation print, and on whether emerging AI concerns change the Fed's growth or inflation assessment.
Semiconductor ETFs took in a record ~$12.7Bn last week (4.3z), above the prior $9.3Bn record from late July. Flows pivoted toward unlevered products: SOXX +$6.5Bn, SOXL +$2.8Bn, SMH +$2.6Bn.

Outside semis, ETF flows were weak, led by Utilities (-2.4z), Materials (-1.4z), Financials (-1.1z) and Staples (-1z). Money Market ETFs flipped to outflows (-$0.9Bn) and gold was sold, with GLD at -$2.3Bn.

CTAs likely sold US equities as short-term signals turned negative on SPX/NDX and volatility rose. They also likely sold Japan equities, sold Bovespa/BRL on this morning's sell-off, flipped short US natgas, remain short metals ex-copper, and are long USD vs DM FX ex-JPY.

CFTC data show asset managers cut VIX shorts (2.1z) after the Oct 16 intraday VIX spike and rotated out of UST 2y-10y into Ultra Bond futures. Leveraged funds cut RTY shorts (+3z), sold VIX (-1.9z) and added to Ultra Bond shorts (-2.9z).
Reuters reports a US-Canada deal may ease US tariffs on Canadian autos (currently 25%) and steel (up to 50%).

Iran hosted Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey for talks on Oct 26 with no deal, and talks continue. Trump said he is nearing a decision on Iran, negotiate or continue attacks, as a third aircraft carrier nears the region. If Trump returns to negotiation, JPM expects a broad rally led by Tech and Cyclicals ex-Energy.

Last week the Recession L/S basket (JPRECES) returned 3.4% and the Stagflation L/S basket (JP9STAGP) returned 1.5%, even though 1Y and 2Y inflation breakevens and bond yields fell. Oil rose for a fourth consecutive week.
The prior monetization menu stands, and the desk would consider adding hedges via longs in oil/Energy equities and long vol.
Senate race moves ahead of Nov 3 midterms: Alaska toward the GOP, Maine toward Democrats, Ohio toward Democrats after the fallout from an attack ad by Ramaswamy.

Morning snapshot: SPX +0.1%, NDX +0.1%, WTI $102.17, gold $3,997 (below $4k, a level thought to act as support), 10Y at 4.984%, VIX 18.25, and USD at a new 52-week high. Memory leads pre-market (DRAM +2.1%) and software is weaker.

earnings_insights: Roughly a quarter of the SPX has reported Q3 2026 earnings with no dips to the pre-season forecast of ~13% revenue growth, ~30% EPS growth and ~15% margins (JPM, basis not specified in the note).

Oct 27 is a heavy earnings day: V, HOOD, PYPL, JBLU and RCL give macro read-through. Other reports before the open include BA, KO, UPS, FCX, GLW and SHW, and after the close include ENPH, STX, TER and WM.
Hyperscaler and MegaCap Tech earnings are due this week: MSFT and GOOGL on Oct 28 after the close, AMZN and INTC on Oct 29 after the close. These are the next catalysts for the AI trade.
JetBlue shares fell to a new low ahead of its earnings (Bloomberg link).

risk_factors: Iran escalation, with Iran threatening regional targets if bombing resumes.
Hawkish Fed with a bias to hike, possible dissents, and Fed-induced volatility extending into next week.
Positioning has not fully washed out.
Emerging AI concerns could affect the Fed's growth or inflation assessment.
Midterm elections on Nov 3 and the Nov 1 trade truce expiry.
CTA de-risking in US and Japan equities as volatility rose.
vol_and_positioning: VIX is 18.25. The note says no complete positioning washout has occurred despite Fear sentiment.
Asset managers cut VIX shorts (2.1z) after the Oct 16 intraday VIX spike, and leveraged funds sold VIX (-1.9z).
Volatility ETFs saw outflows (-0.8z) and defined outcome ETFs drew inflows ($0.9Bn, 1.3z).
Levered ETFs took in ~$4.3Bn (1.7z), led by SOXL (+$2.8Bn), TQQQ (+$1.3Bn) and SOXS (+$0.8Bn).
Liquid alts had their first weekly outflows in ~3 months (-1.5z), mainly managed futures.
Large net futures buying (>1.5z) in S&P 500, FTSE 100, TAIEX, UST Long Bond, UK 10y and copper. Large net selling (<-1.5z) in Dow Jones, SMI, China A50, NIFTY and CAD.
geopolitical: Iran hosted Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey for talks with no deal, and Iran said it would sign any potential MoU.

Trump is nearing a decision on Iran between negotiation and continued attacks, and a third US aircraft carrier is approaching the region. Iran has said new bombing would lead it to target the region, including Israel and the UAE.
Reuters reports a deal may ease US tariffs on Canadian autos and steel.
The UK and EU are discussing closer alignment, including freedom of labor movement (The Times), with a summit on Nov 20.
The one-year US-China trade truce expires Nov 1, and a separate item says the truce has been extended through January 20, 2027 (NBC).
Brazil held a runoff election on Oct 25, and Israel holds a legislative election on Oct 27.
